body.statement: Can \(\text{CertHandle}\) be completed into an output-sensitive, data-based initializer and canonical labeling rule which, on every regular noncyclic finite stratum, returns disjoint certified neighborhoods containing all and only admissible branches exactly once, remains unchanged under perturbations smaller than an explicit separation margin from every excluded branch, and supports simultaneous branchwise confidence regions with asymptotic coverage at least \(1-\alpha\)?
body.justification: The population classification and local delta method do not themselves locate, certify, or stably label every empirical branch.
body.gap: HauensteinSottile2012 certifies supplied approximate roots of square polynomial systems, but does not eliminate snapshot stabilizers, prove completeness of all roots, or certify matrix inequalities and logarithm cuts; ChernozhukovHongTamer2007 covers set-valued criteria without this finite-branch labeling problem.
body.consumer: A complete implementation can replace initialization-sensitive local optimization by certified reporting of every common-noise explanation and its confidence region.

obligation.what_is_open: Construct an explicit output-sensitive algorithm which, from perturbed moments rather than exact spectral and Gram equalities, finds every regular noncyclic empirical branch, certifies completeness and admissibility exactly once, and assigns canonical labels with a computable positive separation radius and simultaneous coverage control.
obligation.obstruction: The certification handle specifies root certification only after approximate roots and an eliminated zero-dimensional system have been supplied. It contains neither a globally complete root-isolation procedure nor a quantitative lower bound separating all raw roots and all excluded roots from stability, logarithm-cut, Stein, and covariance-positivity boundaries. Regularity \(\gamma_W>0\) is local and does not provide those global margins; an excluded branch may lie on an admissibility boundary, so the requested model-count stability cannot hold uniformly on every stated regular finite stratum without an additional separation regime or a boundary-aware set-valued rule.
obligation.attempted: The block sign enumeration was used as a population initializer, and the residual score was linearized at each enumerated branch. This proves a smooth local estimator whenever an isolating neighborhood is already known, but applying exact eigenspace or probe-Gram tests to empirical moments fails almost surely, while local contraction and Smale-style certification certify only roots already targeted and do not establish exhaustion of all roots or a positive distance to excluded branches.
obligation.partial_result: The frozen results already give a complete population enumeration on every finite stratum: \(\text{thm:block-certificate}\) produces the \(2^q\) raw sign completions, \(\text{thm:admissible-fiber}\) filters them exactly, and \(\text{thm:branchwise-inference}\) gives a unique smooth residual estimator in a sufficiently small neighborhood of each regular branch.  For any fixed population instance whose raw branches are mutually separated and whose excluded branches are also separated strictly from every stability, logarithm-cut, and covariance-positivity boundary, compactness of the finite list gives a positive but presently implicit minimum of those separations.  What is not supplied is a data-based, output-sensitive procedure that finds and certifies every empirical neighborhood and computes a valid lower bound for this minimum uniformly over all regular noncyclic finite strata.
